name: Gants
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Daniels, Don (2015), UCSB dissertation reconstructing the Sogeram languages, includes Gants material (cited on Glottolog gant1244; PDF not reachable)

sources.note: No linguistic detail: location, c. 3,000 speakers, 2012 work with two consultants in Madang town, recordings deposited at PARADISEC.

sources.citation: Daniels, Don Roger. 2015. A Reconstruction of Proto-Sogeram: Phonology, Lexicon, and Morphosyntax. PhD dissertation, University of California, Santa Barbara. Appendix 6 'Gants Grammar Sketch' pp. 987-1083 (PDF 1012-1108); phonology sec. 6.2 pp. 989-993 (PDF 1014-1018). = Glottolog ref 469265.
sources.note: Sec. 6.2 read in full: consonant/vowel inventories, plosive allophony, borrowed /r/, glide-vowel syllabification, status of /ɨ/, diphthongs, morphophonemics (6.2.1) -- no statement of where stress falls, no accent/tone remark. Only p. 992 (PDF 1017): 'other vowels will often be centralized to [ɨ] in unstressed syllables or in fast speech.. which can make determining the phonemic quality of an unstressed vowel challenging' (presupposes stressed vs unstressed syllables, gives no rule). Whole-dissertation a full-text search for stress/accent: only p. 72 (PDF 97, Mand *a-centering) 'Further resea…

sources.citation: Z'graggen, J. A. 1971. Classificatory and typological studies in languages of the Madang District. Pacific Linguistics C-19. Canberra: ANU. Gantj = language no. 85, p. 95.
sources.note: Zero hits for 'stress' in the whole volume; Gantj appears only in the census table (pop. 3,520) and a classification note ('collected only a very brief wordlist from Gantj speakers in Madang'; Wurm 1961b, Biggs 1963: 16, Pawley 1966: 3 relate it to Karam).

sources.citation: Usher, Timothy. New Guinea World: 'Gants' (Santa Fe Institute; DokuWiki page, last modified 2024).
sources.note: Phonology section restates Daniels 2015: 989 (14-16 consonants, 6 vowels, 5 diphthongs, stop allophony); nothing on stress. Lists sources: Biggs 1949 'Gaj' vocabulary (unobtained), Aufenanger 1960, Scholtz 1965 SIL vocabulary, Pawley 1992 vocabulary (unobtained), Daniels 2015, 2017, 2020 (unobtained).

sources.citation: Daniels, Don. 2020. Grammatical Reconstruction: The Sogeram Languages of New Guinea (Trends in Linguistics. Studies and Monographs 333). Berlin: De Gruyter Mouton.
sources.note: Comparative-historical monograph; the only post-2015 book-length treatment of the family with Gants data. Chapter 2 (the languages) may carry per-language phonological notes that supersede the 2015 sketch, though the 2015 sketch by the same author is silent on stress so the odds of a placement rule are low.

sources.citation: Daniels, Don. 2017. Gants is a Sogeram language. Language & Linguistics in Melanesia 35: 82-93. ISSN 0023-1959.
sources.note: Nothing: no 'stress', 'accent', 'tone' or 'prosod' in the text. Sec. 2 (pp. 83-85) reviews prior documentation (Aufenanger 1960: 249 c. 20 words; Scholtz 1965 SIL wordlist; Z'graggen 1971: 95 'very brief wordlist'; Pawley 1992 wordlist) and classification history; secs. 3-4 give sound correspondences, cognates and morphology linking Gants to Sogeram and Kursav.

sources.citation: Z'graggen, J. A. 1975. The Madang-Adelbert Range Sub-Phylum. In Wurm (ed.), New Guinea area languages and language study 1: 569-612. Pacific Linguistics C-38.
sources.note: Gants appears only as 'K2 Gants' in a language-list table; no phonology.
sources.venue: New Guinea area languages and language study
